name: Anti-Aliasing
longDescription:
Removes the stair-stepping — "jaggies" — that appears along diagonal edges. Every method works by re-interpolating the frame with an edge-directed kernel and keeping the smoother result, so the edge is rebuilt rather than blurred.

Use it after deinterlacing and after upscaling, which are the two things that create the stepping. It runs before sharpening on purpose: sharpening a stair-stepped edge makes the steps more visible, not less. On a source with no diagonal detail it does nothing but cost time.

methods.name: daa
methods.description: Best first choice. Interpolates both fields and averages them — gentle, and rarely damages anything

methods.name: santiag
methods.description: Stronger, with separate horizontal and vertical strength so it can be aimed at one axis. Slower

methods.name: SangNom
methods.description: The sharpest: rebuilds edges at twice the size with SangNom, then scales back down. Slower than daa on HD sources, since it works at twice the size. Strong enough to thin line art slightly, which suits anime more than live action

ui.label: Strength
ui.description: How hard SangNom smooths along the edges it finds. 48 is the plugin's default; 0 still rebuilds the edges but without smoothing them
